context: Attribute names with labels, levels, role, subsystem, clinical description, physical/physiological mechanism, and directional dependency hints (known upstream drivers and downstream effects) — structured to support causal discovery without fully specifying the DAG.

variables.name: CVP
variables.label: Central venous pressure
variables.description: Right atrial / vena cava pressure; reflects right-heart preload.
variables.mechanism: CVP is determined by the left ventricular volume state (LVV) — which sets overall system filling — and by left ventricular failure (LVF) which backs up pressure through the pulmonary and systemic venous circuits. It is a pure measurement leaf; its value is observed and used for clinical alarms but it does not cause other modeled variables.

variables.name: PCWP
variables.label: Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure
variables.description: Left atrial pressure surrogate; reflects left-heart preload and congestion.
variables.mechanism: PCWP reflects left ventricular filling volume (LVV) and is elevated by left ventricular failure (LVF) through backward pressure transmission. Like CVP, it is an observational leaf that does not cause other variables but is essential for diagnosing LVF and hypovolemia.

variables.name: HIST
variables.label: Patient history flag
variables.description: Prior relevant cardiac or clinical history.
variables.mechanism: Root node with no modeled parents. Encodes baseline patient risk: a positive history raises the prior probability of LVF and other chronic pathologies. Its causal influence propagates solely through LVF.

variables.name: TPR
variables.label: Total peripheral resistance
variables.description: Systemic vascular resistance; determines afterload.
variables.mechanism: TPR is driven by catecholamine level (CCHL, which raises vascular tone via alpha-adrenergic stimulation) and by anaphylaxis (APL, which causes massive vasodilation reducing TPR). TPR jointly determines blood pressure (BP = CO × TPR) and influences stroke volume through afterload effects.

variables.name: BP
variables.label: Blood pressure
variables.description: Systemic arterial pressure; product of CO and TPR.
variables.mechanism: BP is determined by the interaction of cardiac output (CO) and total peripheral resistance (TPR). Hypotension arises from low CO (e.g., LVF, hypovolemia) and/or low TPR (anaphylaxis). BP feeds the HR-BP derived monitoring index (HRBP) but does not directly cause other physiological variables.

variables.name: CO
variables.label: Cardiac output
variables.description: Heart rate × stroke volume; total blood flow per minute.
variables.mechanism: CO is the product of HR and STKV. Low CO triggers the ERLO alarm and is a primary determinant of BP. It is the central node linking the heart-rate pathway and the stroke-volume pathway.

variables.name: HRBP
variables.label: Heart rate / blood pressure index
variables.description: Monitoring index combining HR and BP; detects haemodynamically significant HR changes.
variables.mechanism: Derived from the true underlying heart rate (HR) and blood pressure (BP). An abnormal HRBP alarm is raised when HR deviates from what BP would predict (e.g., compensatory tachycardia in hypotension). Terminal monitoring node — no downstream modeled effects.

variables.name: HREK
variables.label: Heart rate from EKG
variables.description: EKG-derived heart rate observation.
variables.mechanism: Observed HR from the EKG monitor. It reflects the true HR but is corrupted by electrocautery artefact (ERCA). When ERCA=TRUE, HREK may not accurately represent HR. Terminal monitoring leaf — no downstream effects.

variables.name: HRSA
variables.label: Heart rate / oxygen saturation index
variables.description: Monitoring index combining HR and arterial oxygen saturation.
variables.mechanism: Derived from HR and SAO2. Flags HR abnormalities in the context of hypoxia (e.g., tachycardia as a compensatory response to low SAO2). Terminal monitoring leaf — no downstream effects.

variables.name: PAP
variables.label: Pulmonary artery pressure
variables.description: Pressure in the pulmonary artery; elevated by PE or LVF.
variables.mechanism: PAP is raised by two independent mechanisms: pulmonary embolus (PMB) obstructing the pulmonary vasculature, and left ventricular failure (LVF) causing backward congestion into the pulmonary circulation. Terminal hemodynamic leaf — not a cause of other modeled variables.

variables.name: SAO2
variables.label: Arterial oxygen saturation
variables.description: Arterial haemoglobin-O2 saturation; key hypoxaemia indicator.
variables.mechanism: SAO2 is determined by pulmonary venous saturation (PVS) and intrapulmonary shunt (SHNT). High shunt reduces SAO2 even with adequate alveolar ventilation. SAO2 feeds monitoring indices HRSA and is a key downstream oxygenation signal.

variables.name: FIO2
variables.label: Fraction of inspired oxygen
variables.description: Ventilator-controlled O2 fraction; root input to oxygenation.
variables.mechanism: Root node (no clinical parents in the model). FIO2 is set by the clinician/ventilator. It directly determines the oxygen available for alveolar gas exchange, influencing pulmonary venous saturation (PVS). Low FIO2 propagates to hypoxaemia via PVS and SAO2.

variables.name: PRSS
variables.label: Breathing circuit pressure
variables.description: Observed airway circuit pressure.
variables.mechanism: PRSS is driven by the ventilation present at the tube level (VTUB): higher VTUB produces higher circuit pressure. ZERO pressure indicates disconnection or zero machine output. Terminal observation — not a cause of other modeled variables.

variables.name: ECO2
variables.label: Expired CO2
variables.description: End-tidal CO2; reflects alveolar ventilation and CO2 washout.
variables.mechanism: ECO2 is produced by alveolar ventilation (VALV) removing CO2 from the blood. ZERO ECO2 indicates no gas exchange (esophageal intubation, circuit disconnection). Terminal observation leaf.

variables.name: MINV
variables.label: Minute ventilation (observed)
variables.description: Measured total ventilation per minute.
variables.mechanism: MINV reflects the ventilation actually delivered through the lung pathway (VLNG). It deviates from VMCH due to tube or circuit faults. Terminal observation leaf — used for alarms.

variables.name: MVS
variables.label: Minute ventilation set (target)
variables.description: Clinician-prescribed minute ventilation target.
variables.mechanism: Root node set by the clinician. Drives the ventilator machine output (VMCH). The entire ventilation delivery cascade begins at MVS.

variables.name: HYP
variables.label: Hypovolemia
variables.description: Reduced circulating blood volume; primary preload depressor.
variables.mechanism: Root node. Hypovolemia reduces left ventricular filling volume (LVV), which in turn reduces stroke volume and cardiac output. It is the primary mechanism behind low CVP, low PCWP, and low CO in the absence of cardiac disease.

variables.name: LVF
variables.label: Left ventricular failure
variables.description: Impaired LV contractility; reduces output and elevates filling pressures.
variables.mechanism: Root node (modulated by HIST). LVF reduces stroke volume (STKV) through impaired contractility, raises left-sided filling pressures (PCWP, CVP), and elevates pulmonary artery pressure (PAP). It is the dominant cause of the combined low-output/high-filling-pressure pattern.

variables.name: APL
variables.label: Anaphylaxis
variables.description: Severe allergic reaction causing systemic vasodilation.
variables.mechanism: Root node. Anaphylaxis massively reduces total peripheral resistance (TPR) through histamine-mediated vasodilation, causing severe hypotension. It may also trigger a reflex catecholamine surge (CCHL). Produces the low-TPR, low-BP pattern distinct from hypovolemia.

variables.name: ANES
variables.label: Insufficient anesthesia / analgesia
variables.description: Inadequate anaesthetic depth; triggers sympathetic catecholamine release.
variables.mechanism: Root node. Pain or awareness under anaesthesia activates the sympathetic nervous system, raising circulating catecholamine levels (CCHL). CCHL then elevates HR and TPR. ANES is causally upstream of all sympathetic haemodynamic effects.

variables.name: PMB
variables.label: Pulmonary embolus
variables.description: Pulmonary vascular obstruction; raises PAP and creates V/Q mismatch.
variables.mechanism: Root node. PMB simultaneously obstructs pulmonary vasculature (raising PAP) and creates ventilation-perfusion mismatch (raising intrapulmonary shunt SHNT), thereby reducing oxygenation. The dual PAP+SAO2 pattern is pathognomonic.

variables.name: INT
variables.label: Intubation status
variables.description: Endotracheal tube placement; determines whether ventilation reaches the trachea.
variables.mechanism: Root node. ESOPHAGEAL placement means all ventilation from the tube (VTUB) enters the stomach — lung ventilation (VLNG) collapses to ZERO. ONESIDED (main-stem intubation) ventilates only one lung, reducing effective VLNG. Correct tube placement is necessary for any ventilation to reach the alveoli.

variables.name: KINK
variables.label: Kinked breathing tube
variables.description: Physical obstruction of the ETT; blocks gas flow.
variables.mechanism: Root node. Kinking obstructs the endotracheal tube, reducing tube ventilation (VTUB). In combination with circuit disconnection (DISC) or misplaced tube (INT), multiple faults can summate to zero ventilation. KINK is causally upstream of VTUB.

variables.name: DISC
variables.label: Circuit disconnection
variables.description: Breathing circuit separation; eliminates gas delivery.
variables.mechanism: Root node. Disconnection breaks the gas path, reducing tube ventilation (VTUB) to ZERO regardless of machine output (VMCH). The circuit integrity must be intact for MVS-set ventilation to be delivered.

variables.name: LVV
variables.label: Left ventricular end-diastolic volume
variables.description: LV preload volume; the Frank-Starling input to stroke volume.
variables.mechanism: LVV is set by filling status (HYP reduces it) and by LVF (which impairs emptying and may raise residual volume). By the Frank-Starling law, LVV directly determines stroke volume (STKV). It is also the primary driver of venous filling pressures CVP and PCWP.

variables.name: STKV
variables.label: Stroke volume
variables.description: Volume ejected per beat; determined by preload, contractility, and afterload.
variables.mechanism: STKV is determined by LVV (preload via Frank-Starling), LVF (contractility impairment), and TPR (afterload). STKV is a direct multiplicative factor in cardiac output (CO = HR × STKV). It is the central integrating pathophysiology node for all causes of low output.

variables.name: CCHL
variables.label: Catecholamine level
variables.description: Circulating epinephrine/norepinephrine; drives HR and vascular tone.
variables.mechanism: CCHL is elevated by insufficient anaesthesia (ANES) via sympathetic activation and by low cardiac output states (ERLO) through the baroreceptor reflex. Elevated CCHL raises heart rate (HR) via chronotropic stimulation and raises total peripheral resistance (TPR) via alpha-adrenergic vasoconstriction.

variables.name: ERLO
variables.label: Error / low output flag
variables.description: Low-output monitoring alarm; triggered by low CO.
variables.mechanism: ERLO is triggered when cardiac output (CO) falls below a threshold. It then feeds back into catecholamine release (CCHL) as a reflex response to low perfusion, creating an indirect feedback loop between CO and HR/TPR.

variables.name: HR
variables.label: Heart rate
variables.description: Intrinsic heart rate; driven by catecholamines and autonomic tone.
variables.mechanism: HR is driven by catecholamine level (CCHL). It is one of the two multiplicative determinants of cardiac output (CO = HR × STKV). HR also feeds three monitoring indices: HRBP (with BP), HREK (with EKG noise from ERCA), and HRSA (with SAO2).

variables.name: ERCA
variables.label: Electrocautery in use
variables.description: Electrosurgical cautery; corrupts EKG signal.
variables.mechanism: Root node. When ERCA=TRUE, the high-frequency electrical interference corrupts the EKG-derived heart rate reading (HREK), potentially masking true HR abnormalities. ERCA does not affect the underlying physiology — only the measurement accuracy of HREK.

variables.name: SHNT
variables.label: Intrapulmonary shunt
variables.description: Fraction of blood bypassing ventilated alveoli; causes refractory hypoxaemia.
variables.mechanism: SHNT is elevated by pulmonary embolus (PMB), which creates V/Q mismatch, and by alveolar ventilation deficits (VALV). High shunt reduces arterial oxygen saturation (SAO2) in a manner unresponsive to FIO2 increases.

variables.name: PVS
variables.label: Pulmonary venous oxygen saturation
variables.description: O2 saturation of blood leaving the lungs; set by FIO2 and alveolar ventilation.
variables.mechanism: PVS is determined by the fraction of inspired oxygen (FIO2) and effective alveolar ventilation (VALV). Together they determine the alveolar PO2 and hence haemoglobin saturation of pulmonary venous blood. PVS feeds into arterial saturation (SAO2) modified by shunt.

variables.name: ACO2
variables.label: Arterial CO2
variables.description: Arterial PaCO2; inversely related to alveolar ventilation.
variables.mechanism: ACO2 is determined by alveolar ventilation (VALV): hyperventilation lowers ACO2; hypoventilation raises it. ACO2 is a terminal measurement leaf in the oxygenation pathway and used as a clinical indicator of ventilatory adequacy.

variables.name: VALV
variables.label: Alveolar ventilation
variables.description: Gas exchange ventilation at the alveoli; lung ventilation minus dead space.
variables.mechanism: VALV is derived from lung ventilation (VLNG) minus anatomical dead space. It is the final effective-ventilation node that simultaneously drives CO2 removal (ACO2, ECO2), oxygenation (PVS), and shunt-related effects on SAO2.

variables.name: VLNG
variables.label: Lung ventilation
variables.description: Total ventilation reaching both lungs; the penultimate ventilation node.
variables.mechanism: VLNG is determined by tube ventilation (VTUB) modified by intubation status (INT). ESOPHAGEAL intubation forces VLNG to ZERO; ONESIDED intubation halves effective ventilation. Normal VLNG then propagates to alveolar ventilation (VALV) and to the observed MINV measurement.

variables.name: VTUB
variables.label: Tube ventilation
variables.description: Gas flow through the ETT; can be blocked by kinking or disconnection.
variables.mechanism: VTUB is the ventilation that reaches the endotracheal tube from the machine (VMCH) after circuit faults (KINK, DISC) are applied. KINK or DISC independently reduce VTUB to ZERO or LOW. VTUB then determines both lung ventilation (VLNG) and circuit pressure (PRSS).

variables.name: VMCH
variables.label: Ventilator machine output
variables.description: Tidal/minute volume delivered by the ventilator; set by MVS.
variables.mechanism: VMCH is driven by the set minute ventilation (MVS). It is the first node in the ventilation delivery chain before the gas encounters circuit faults. Normal VMCH with a fault downstream (DISC, KINK, INT) produces the classic pattern of machine delivering but patient not receiving ventilation.
